assign.outcome:
**Landed: /layouts/labs/trees/** — a seeded label generator (`a`, `a1`, `a1a` …) drawn three ways in plain flexbox/grid CSS, no canvas, no SVG, no coordinate math anywhere: a family tree (centred flex rows), a flow chart (a grid, `align-items: center`), a brainstorm map (two mirrored flow charts either side of a centred root). Click any node to fold/unfold and scroll it into view; each drawing gets its own real `requestFullscreen()` button (a swipe becomes pan-only inside it, pinch-zoom left to the browser on purpose); under 40rem the drawings switch from centred to top-aligned, fixing the owner's own "first column is empty" problem — measured on a real overflowing tree, not guessed: centred the root sat 465px down inside a 946px scroll area (off-screen at rest); top-aligned, 14px down.

**Links** — [the lab](/layouts/labs/trees/) · [readme](/layouts/labs/trees/readme/) · [doc/decisions.md](/layouts/labs/trees/doc/decisions.md) (every alternative considered, the mobile-framing numbers, a bug the proof caught) · linked from [/layouts/labs/](/layouts/labs/)'s own wall (Six → Seven labs).

**The generator** — written fresh (`gen.js`, 20 lines past a copied `rng()`): `core/Page/generator/gen.js` was read first but draws PAGE trees (`tabs vtabs list wall prose`), never a label, so it did not fit.

**Verified headless**, `PORT=8130`, zero console errors throughout: page load at 400/1280/1920; a depth-3/breadth-3 tree shot per drawing at 1280 and 400; fold then unfold a node (`aria-expanded` false → true); `demo.steps()`'s three-step tutorial completed in the right order (a real bug — the fold/unfold event names were swapped — was caught by this proof, not by eye, and fixed); real fullscreen entered and exited with the icon and `document.fullscreenElement` both correct; the parent page links to and opens the card cleanly.

**Left deliberately** — no "add an item" editing UI (the owner's own words describe the eventual product; this is the generator/drawing proof asked for first) · no custom pinch-zoom (the browser's own, on purpose — `pan-x pan-y` would have removed it) · clicking a node re-centres it but does not re-crop the pan area to just that subtree (a further interaction, not a gap in what was asked).
